warning_signs_missed: A client asking 'is this complaint solved?' for the third time about the same issue is an active churn risk that week. We answered 'Yes all solved' with no evidence and she quit eighteen hours later.

We told her to switch off the paid traffic she was funding herself and then never replaced it. Every subsequent complaint she raised was downstream of that single decision, and it was never revisited.

Five requests over two weeks to rotate the passwords on her accounts - one of them immediately after she reported a compromise - were never actioned or confirmed. Ignoring a client's own security request destroys trust faster than anything else on this file.
'Why when i ask no one answer' (2026-06-27) is an explicit complaint about responsiveness on day ten. It was never treated as a signal.

Her whales losing trust in her persona (2026-06-30) was the first commercial symptom, was correctly diagnosed by the account manager, agreed for action the same day, and then never mentioned by anyone again.

Two fans paid $1,700 for work we sold without briefing her; she raised Jake's undelivered call unprompted on 2026-08-01 and nobody has mentioned it since. Unresolved fan liabilities sit under the relationship as a constant irritant.

The same account-number change that was pushed to other clients went to a crypto-only payer who had already been sent a wrong-network address - a client already primed to distrust our payment instructions.
She never once refused to pay, disputed an invoice or went hostile, so her churn had no billing-side warning; all the signal was in the service thread and nobody was reading it.
Twenty-eight messages were deleted from this chat, four of them inside the Jake dispute, her compromise report and the final-invoice thread. Nobody ever noticed, explained or archived them.
A team member posting 'Hi' into the group 15 days after the client left proves churn does not propagate internally - the same failure that let billing chase other departed clients.
